verdicts.why: In Hot Potato Soup, Ivanov tells Shockley to remove Radcliffe and Aida; Aida kills Babikov and slowly crushes Shockley's hand. She does not spare him; the proposed text and card lines match.
In Self Control, Aida slits Radcliffe's wrists, which traps his mind in the Framework as his body dies: one act, with no later killing by her.

Radcliffe is only mentioned in What If... (S4#16). In Identity and Change (S4#17), Radcliffe tries to make the Doctor remember who he really is; the Doctor kills Agnes and Radcliffe is taken prisoner to the Triskelion.

Nothing in the current text is false. Jemma distrusts Aida, Radcliffe's plan puts her friends in the Framework, she goes in after them (S4#16) and confronts him on Ogygia (S4#17). This is a fuller retelling, not a fix of an error.

value.text: Davis helps pull Fitz out of the chamber where Aida, now the human Ophelia, attacks him. He keeps shooting her so Piper can get Fitz away, but her wounds heal and she leaves him for dead.

verdicts.why: Piper shoots Aida once and Davis empties his gun to buy them time, then Aida heals and leaves him for dead. 'Badly hurt' gives away that he survives, which is only shown in S5#12.

In S5#11 the masked leader of the androids is shown only as Hale's daughter. Hale's Hydra allegiance comes out at the end of S5#14 and in Rise and Shine (S5#15), so 'Hydra's young enforcer' gives the reveal away early.

In the 1990s flashback of Rise and Shine, Whitehall picks Hale to bear Hydra's future leader. Ruby is raised while Whitehall is still alive (he dies in 2014), so 'long after his death' is wrong. The fix is right, though the checker's 'about 28 years' age figure is off.

Enoch offers Jemma up to Atarah in The Other Thing (S6#5). In Inescapable (S6#6), Atarah tells him to pick his people or his friends; he picks his friends, knocks out the Chronicoms and escapes with Fitz and Simmons.

Enoch offering up Jemma, and Fitz's anger at him, both happen in The Other Thing (S6#5). In S6#6, Enoch warns Atarah, chooses his friends, deactivates the Chronicoms and teleports out with Fitz and Simmons.

The text is true. The first sentence is past-tense backstory (S4#3), and the S6#13 events are right: Simmons injects May with a healing formula and puts her in a cryo-freeze chamber. Rewording it is not fixing an error.

The current text holds up. Sarge swings his sword at Daisy in the truck during their truce (S6#8). In New Life, Daisy comes for revenge over May, and her quake exposes his true form so Mack can cut him down. The proposed 'quakes have no effect' is wrong.

value.text: Sibyl hears from her Hunters that their plan to kill Freddy in 1931 failed because S.H.I.E.L.D. saved him.

verdicts.why: The attempt on Freddy happens in S7#1-2. In S7#3, Sibyl first appears, and Luke and Abel discuss with her the failed plan to kill him. The proposed 'new plan in 1955' is Helius and does not involve Freddy, so it is dropped.

In After, Before (S7#8), Daisy never meets or hears of Kora. In Stolen (S7#10), Daisy learns that Kora is her half-sister who died before Daisy was born in the original timeline, and Kora tells Coulson she wanted to meet her sister.
Deke's page says that once captured, Garrett tortures him for Fitz's whereabouts and he gives nothing. Garrett then tortures him in front of Simmons to make her talk. The current text is accurate.

value.on_b_card_about_a: Sousa's love, who first meets him at Area 51 in 1955.

verdicts.why: The title stays: in The End Is at Hand (S7#12), Sousa stops Daisy and kisses her before she goes after her friends, so S7#12 is a real turn and moving the stage to S7#9 is not needed. The b-card is wrong, though: they first meet at Area 51 in S7#3, before the team saves him.

value.title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S7#3
value.text: Posing as a CIA agent at Area 51, Daisy wins Sousa over and gets him to take her to her captured teammates, who then lock him in their cell.
value.on_a_card_about_b: An SSR agent Daisy wins over at Area 51.
value.on_b_card_about_a: An agent who poses as CIA to win him over at Area 51.

verdicts.why: Their connection clearly starts in Alien Commies from the Future! (S7#3), where Daisy, undercover, wins Sousa over. Under the rules it gets a stage there. The partner stage stays at S7#12 (see n14).
In Code of the Streets, Tone's contact will not give the location at first. Then Tone and Shades meet Turk in person and he tells them he saw Chico at the barbershop. He does not text it.

value.title: Luke Cage S1#1
value.text: Luke washes dishes at Cottonmouth's club, Harlem's Paradise. Filling in at the bar, he brings Cottonmouth drinks and turns down his job offer.
value.on_a_card_about_b: A dishwasher at Harlem's Paradise who turns down his job offer.
value.on_b_card_about_a: The owner of Harlem's Paradise, where Luke washes dishes.

verdicts.why: They deal with each other in Moment of Truth (S1#1), where Luke works at the club and Cottonmouth offers him a job, so the connection gets a stage there. The S1#3 text is true (Luke's former employer, enemies after Pop's death), so it stays.
